text: Deployed bytecode is permanent, except for one deliberate exception. A proxy holds the storage and the address users interact with, while a separate implementation contract holds the logic.
delegatecall runs the implementation's code inside the proxy's own storage context. Upgrading means pointing the proxy at a new implementation address — the proxy's address and storage never change.

All three patterns use delegatecall underneath — they differ in who's allowed to trigger an upgrade. Transparent checks the caller in the proxy. UUPS puts that check in the implementation. Beacon upgrades many proxies at once.

No constructor — an initialize function instead, since a constructor's state changes never apply to the proxy's storage. authorizeUpgrade must be protected, or anyone can point your proxy at malicious logic.
A proxy reintroduces exactly the risk immutability was protecting against. That's why multisig-controlled deployments matter even more here — authorizeUpgrade should almost never be a single key.
